meta.what: The rules the forge works by, as ruled by the project owner. Each rule names the proposal in docs/decisions-log.md that set it.
meta.status: Provisional until the first numbered release.

how_a_new_word_is_made.rule: A new word starts from a sentence, not from a word list. A proposal must include the dragon-language sentence the word is needed for.
how_a_new_word_is_made.example: The question words came from a sentence the owner wanted to say: Why did you do that?

how_a_new_word_is_made.rule: Before coining, try what the language already has: an existing word, a phrase, a form built on an existing family, or a compound.
Where English has two words for what the language treats as one idea, no new word is made.
how_a_new_word_is_made.example: No word may be coined for 'me': zu'u is both 'I' and 'me' (grammar ruling G06-pronouns).

how_a_new_word_is_made.rule: A coined word is defined by how it is used, with a short explanation and examples, not by a single English word.

The first batch of missing words comes from the course's own conversation scenes: the scenes are written, and the words they cannot be written without are brought to the owner. Lists of basic English concepts are a cross-check, not the to-do list.
No word is borrowed from English or any other real language.
how_a_new_word_is_made.owner_words: We don't borrow words from English or other real languages. Maybe daedric but no borrowing from real languages.
how_a_new_word_is_made.note: Borrowing from the game world's own languages is not ruled out and not yet decided. Daedric in the games is an alphabet used to write English, not a stock of words; the game world's languages that do have word lists are others. A word built from game words may by chance look like a real word; that is not borrowing.

what_may_be_built_on.rule: Words graded game, guide or guide website may be used as building parts. Guide-website words carry a single-source mark.
The seven words whose source is untraced (naas, raal, um, unraak, viint, vindahlheim, vos) are kept and usable, labelled 'source untraced'.
Ten later-game words with no recorded meaning are reserved: never given an invented meaning, and their spellings not reused.
A spelling variant is not a separate word and cannot be built on.

form_of_a_new_word.rule: Only the standard spelling is accepted in new writing.
An apostrophe is accepted in two places only: between two u's where the coiner declares a break, and in the possessive endings -i'i and -i'il.
A new verb or adjective is strong (it can also serve as a noun) unless a separate noun for the same idea exists.
A word may be used in every role the word-type system allows.
The pronunciation of a new word is worked out from its spelling by the rule in pronunciation.json. Stress goes on the root the coiner declares; for a new root, on the first syllable.

community_vocabulary.rule: Things created by the community can be kept.
community_vocabulary.owner_words: we can keep things created by the community... that's how language naturally evolves

community_vocabulary.rule: The retired Thuum.org fan vocabulary is a source of candidates, not a set of accepted words. A fan word comes in through the same door as any other: a sentence that needs it, the checks, the owner's ratification, and credit to its maker.

what_the_app_will_not_have.rule: No automatic translator that turns English sentences into dragon ones word by word. Looking a word up in the dictionary stays.
what_the_app_will_not_have.why: Thuum.org's administrator names the word-for-word translator, with a submission system that promoted finding missing English translations, as what pushed its community toward an English-centred view of the language.

who_decides: Checks decide what may be proposed. Only the owner ratifies. A ratified word never changes its form or meaning; it can only be retired.
